I looked at the spreadsheet description you pasted: Seed, Packets, Borrower, Date out, Date back, with about a third of the Date back cells empty.

Those empty cells are where I'd like to start, because they could mean very different things. Some may be seeds that are genuinely still out. Others may have come back without anyone writing it down. And in many seed libraries, nothing is expected back at all, or what comes back is seed saved from the borrower's own harvest a season later, sometimes a different variety or amount. Each of those calls for a different tool. One would chase overdue loans, one would make check-ins easier to record, and one would track a seed's life from packet to harvest and back to the shelf.

So: when someone borrows a packet today, what does "coming back" actually look like, and what do you wish you knew about those empty rows that you can't tell right now?
